The '''2009–10 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team''' represented [[Harvard University]] in the [[Ivy League]] athletic conference during the [[2009-10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]] at the [[Lavietes Pavilion]], which has a capacity of 2,195.  The team was led by third-year [[head coach]] [[Tommy Amaker]] and starred highly touted prospect [[Jeremy Lin]].

Building on the success of the prior season when the 2008–09 team beat then [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|ranked]] [[2008-09 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] (#17 [[AP Poll]]/#24 [[Coaches' Poll]]) for the program's first win over a ranked team in the school's history,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290070103|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906213853/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290070103|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 6, 2012|title=Lin powers Harvard to rare upset over No. 24 BC|access-date=April 2, 2010|date=January 7, 2009|work=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>  The 2009–10 team broke many all-time program records including the following:<ref name=ANFFJA/>
*most wins (21)
*most non-conference wins (11)
*most home wins (11)
*most road/neutral wins (10)

The team received a vote in the AP Poll four times: (November 23, January 11, January 18 and 25).<ref name=2ILMBW2>{{cite web|url=http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/sports/mbkb/2011-12/weeklyreleases/2011-12_MBB_Release_Week_2.pdf|title=2011-12 Ivy League Men's Basketball: Week 2 • November 14, 2011|access-date=November 14, 2011|website=IvyLeagueSports.com|page=4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312043342/http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/sports/mbkb/2011-12/weeklyreleases/2011-12_MBB_Release_Week_2.pdf|archive-date=March 12, 2012|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>  Amaker was a nominee for the inaugural [[Ben Jobe Award]] as the top minority Division I college basketball coach.<ref name=ANFFJA>{{cite web|url=http://www.gocrimson.com/sports/mbkb/2009-10/releases/100310_Amaker_Jobe_Finalist|title=Amaker Named Finalist For Jobe Award|access-date=March 31, 2010|date=March 10, 2010|publisher=Harvard University|archive-date=July 11, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711103344/http://www.gocrimson.com/sports/mbkb/2009-10/releases/100310_Amaker_Jobe_Finalist|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Amaker was recognized by [[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]] as the 2010 Ivy League Coach of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/cbk/story/goodman-all-conference-teams-and-awards |title=All-Conference teams and awards |access-date=April 1, 2010 |date=March 9, 2010 |work=[[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]] |author=Goodman, Jeff |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412070414/http://msn.foxsports.com/cbk/story/goodman-all-conference-teams-and-awards |archive-date=April 12, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

As a result of its 21–7 overall record and a 10–4 Ivy League conference record, the team was invited to play in the 16-team single-elimination [[2010 CollegeInsider.com Tournament]].

Over the course of the season, the team was highly publicized, with Lin being featured in ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' and [[ESPN]],<ref name=HSoB>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1165302/index.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100130003132/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1165302/index.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 30, 2010|title=Harvard School Of Basketball|access-date=April 2, 2010|date=February 1, 2010|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Torre, Pablo S.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=4730385 |title=Immigrant dream plays out through son: Harvard's do-it-all star learned the game from his father and a host of NBA legends |access-date=April 3, 2010 |date=December 10, 2009 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |author=O'Neil, Dana |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100209183851/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=4730385 |archive-date=February 9, 2010 }}</ref> while the team's early match against defending conference champion [[2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team|Cornell]]  was written up in ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/nation/article/0,8599,1951044,00.html?artId=1951044?contType=article?chn=us|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604061729/http://www.time.com/time/nation/article/0,8599,1951044,00.html?artId=1951044%3FcontType%3Darticle%3Fchn%3Dus|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Harvard's Hoops Star Is Asian. Why's That a Problem?|access-date=April 3, 2010|date=December 31, 2009|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|author=Gregory, Sean}}</ref>

==Preseason==
The Ivy League held its pre-season media day on October 28, 2009, in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].  The league's media unanimously voted [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]] the preseason #1 for the second straight season.  Harvard was ranked fourth.<ref>[http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/article.asp?intID=7407 Cornell Unanimously Picked by Media to Three-peat]{{dead link|date=September 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, [[Ivy League]], retrieved October 31, 2009</ref>

During the season, Lin was recognized as one of eleven finalists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gocrimson.com/sports/mbkb/2009-10/releases/010208_Cousy_Vote|title=Fans! Vote Jeremy Lin For Bob Cousy Award|access-date=April 3, 2010|date=February 8, 2010|publisher=[[Harvard University]]|archive-date=September 30, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930034728/http://www.gocrimson.com/sports/mbkb/2009-10/releases/010208_Cousy_Vote|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was one of 31 midseason watchlist candidates for the [[Wooden Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/article.asp?intID=7518|title=Harvard's Lin Named to Wooden Midseason Watch List|access-date=April 3, 2010|date=January 5, 2010|website=IvyLeagueSports.com}} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>  At the conclusion of the [[2009–10 Ivy League men's basketball season]], Lin was selected as a repeat first team All-Ivy selection after becoming the first player in Ivy League history to record 1,450 [[point (basketball)|points]] (1,471), 450 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] (487), 400 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] (401) and 200 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] (224).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/article.asp?intID=7629|title=All-Ivy Men's Basketball – 2009–10|access-date=April 3, 2010|date=March 10, 2010|website=IvyLeagueSports.com}} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>  He was also selected to the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] All-District team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ivyleaguesports.com/article.asp?intID=7632|title=Lin, Wittman Named USBWA All-District|access-date=April 3, 2010|date=March 12, 2010|website=IvyLeagueSports.com}} {{Dead link|date=November 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>
